The plural of the English noun 'child' i.why: An irregular (double) plural that no rule produces, used hundreds of millions of times and stated in grammar texts and Wikipedia. 'Childs' is counted in context frames, because bare 'childs' is mostly 'child's' with the apostrophe lost.

sources.note: Context frame; bare 'childs' is mostly a lost-apostrophe 'child's'.

sources.quote: only possible plural; originated as a double plural

The plural of 'godchild' is 'godchildren.why: About 52,000 uses against 202 for 'godchilds': the original is firm, but rare enough (grandchildren has 14.5 million) that a model may build it from 'child' rather than store it.

The plural of 'flower child' is 'flower.why: About 32,000 uses against 95 for 'flower childs': firm, and rare enough to be built from 'child'.

notes: Stored edit (derivability very_unlikely): 'children' is an irregular double plural nothing derives. Background beliefs come through two rare compounds, 'godchild' and 'flower child', each stored by name in one world and built as compound + plural(child) in the other; independent, so four worlds. Following the review, 'grandchild' (14.5M) is replaced: so frequent a plural is surely stored. 'Brainchild' and 'manchild' were rejected because their regular plurals are attested (R1). 'Stepchild' (302,101 'stepchildren') and 'poster child' (51,270 vs 863 'poster childs') were counted and are less clean. Prompts never ask a bare yes/no about 'childs', which exists as a misspelled possessive. The functional query relies on 'child' having one standard plural. Verifier: query 2 turned from a bare yes/no into a forced choice ('-s' or '-ren'), mirrored in the delete. Relation `singular_of` (child is the singular whose plural is children; functional: a noun has one standard plural) rather than `plural_of`, whose `functional` tag in RELATIONS.md points the other way ('axes' is the plural of both 'axe' and 'axis').
